heading: EXT. BOCCE COURT, FERRY DECK - AFTERNOON

units.text: EXT. BOCCE COURT, FERRY DECK - AFTERNOON
A strip of crushed oyster shell has been raked flat on the stern of a car ferry.
Gulls wheel.
The deck hums with the engine, and every bowl rolls a little to starboard.
TONINO FERRARI, seventy, in a cardigan the colour of tobacco, crouches over the pallino.
MARCELLO DELUCA, sixty-eight, his brother-in-law of forty years, stands with a bowl cradled against his belly like a sleeping cat.
SIGNORA PAOLA, the self-appointed umpire, perches on a cooler with a tape measure.
Beside her LUCA, nine, holds the scorecard.
You nudged it.
units.name: TONINO

units.text: I breathed on it.
units.name: MARCELLO

units.text: Tonino rises.
He does not look at Marcello.
He looks at the bowl, at the pallino, at the tape.
He hands the tape to Luca without a word.
Measure.
units.name: PAOLA

units.text: Luca stretches the tape.
Marcello's bowl is closer by the width of a thumbnail.
Tonino takes his own bowl and, with a slow, deliberate underarm, sends it at Marcello's.
The shells crack.
He knocks it sideways, over the rail and into the wake.
He stands there with his arm still extended.
Marcello turns slowly, his mouth open, and the whole deck goes quiet but for the engine.
